text:
lucas-pm: Quick sync: I want to propose a "regional congestion fallback" plan — goal is predictable degradation when a region hits capacity (no customer surprise), and a clear path for VIP opt-outs. High level below.

tara-eng: Sounds good. Can we enumerate fallback actions and rank them by user impact? e.g. 1) latency smoothing (token throttling), 2) quality downgrade (smaller quantized model), 3) reroute to another region, 4) best-effort read-only responses (no hallucination checks).

lucas-pm: Exactly. My ranking: A: non-intrusive (throttle/context trim), B: model downgrade, C: cross-region failover, D: degrade-to-stub. We'll gate each action with flags and a pace limiter.

omar-sre: Telemetry and safety rules: require per-region rolling p95, p99, error-rate, and CPU/GPU saturation. Auto-trigger if p95 > baseline + 200ms for 2m AND region_util > 85% for 1m. Rollback/halt if error_rate > 1.5% for 3m. Also capture sample traces for last 50 requests pre/post fallback.

ivy-ops: Flag knobs (draft):
```
regional_fallback: off | monitor | throttle | downgrade | reroute | degrade
fallback_slice: 0-100
fallback_exempt_tenants: [tenant_ids]
fallback_cooldown_sec: 900
fallback_rate_limit_per_min: 30
```
Keep flags per-region + per-availability-zone where possible.

kevin-sales: Customer ask: large customers want a clear opt-out (no cross-region failover during business hours) or we route them to a reserved pool. They expect pricing for guaranteed non-fallback hours. Need to surface as add-on.

lucas-pm: Product decision: MVP will support `fallback_exempt_tenants` (manual opt-in), and a tag-based `reserved_pool:true` feature to route to dedicated capacity. We'll iterate pricing after legal/sales input.

tara-eng: Canary plan idea: Controlled canary per-region. Steps: shadow detection -> 1% traffic throttle -> 5% -> 20%. Each step waits for stability window (10m for 1%, 20m for 5%, 1h for 20%). Run blind shadow vs baseline to measure quality delta (metric: accept_rate or task-specific score). If delta > threshold, stop. Store evicted request payloads to S3 for analysis.

omar-sre: Add circuit breakers: max_fallbacks_per_region_per_hour = 6; token bucket to ensure at most X evictions/second to avoid cascading. Also include manual 'panic button' in runbook to disable cross-region reroute.

ivy-ops: Launch criteria checklist (proposed):
- Canary no customer-visible regressions for 48h
- Telemetry dashboards: p95/p99 + error-rate + evictions/sec visible
- Runbook and pager playbook published
- API to toggle `fallback_exempt_tenants` available and tested
- Sales/legal sign-off on reserved_pool wording

kevin-sales: I'll start customer comms drafts and pricing options. Need a short FAQ for customers that ask "what happens to my SLA if my region is congested?"

lucas-pm: UX/ops: include a tenant-visibility API: list current fallback state for tenant + last eviction time. That helps support.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: `rollout/regional-fallback/v1` -> canary start 2026-04-01T14:00:00Z (1% eu-west)

tara-eng: I'll author the PRD and the flag spec. Ops, can you validate the cooldown and rate limits?

omar-sre: Will run simulations against traffic replay and push recommended thresholds. Also will add end-to-end test harness to simulate region saturation.

lucas-pm: Great. Let's reconvene after the PRD + runbook are posted. Drop any missing must-haves here.

kevin-sales: One more: add explicit on/off hours for reserved_pool so customers can choose business-hours protection only.

ivy-ops: noted — add `reserved_pool_hours: [09:00-17:00 Europe/Berlin]` to the API schema.
